721990201.text: Ho there, youngster! I do not recognize your face. Did you see the notice as well?

721990203.text: Yes, haha. Does it appear like anyone else nearby is young?

721990204.text: Oh dear, where are my manners?

721990206.text: I believe you must have seen that notice earlier. As you may suspect, I am Saimon Katsumi.

721990207.text: It brings me no small amount of shame to ask outsiders to help me find that useless son of mine...

721990208.text: But please, do tell me if you hear of anything regarding him, alright?

721990209.text: No matter if that little brat is alive, or... *sigh*

721990210.text: Please tell me everything you know truthfully.

721990214.text: It's fine, leave it to us!

721990215.text: Ah yes, youngster. Let me also say that if you're able to enter and exit military camps... you could simply ask that lad's comrades-in-arms.

721990216.text: There's another young lad who joined the army together with him. Ishikawa, I think his name was. A military family's son, and a reliable one at that.

721990217.text: I'm sorry to have kept you here for so long. Still, if you receive any new, don't forget to swing by Konda Village and inform me.

721990218.text: Alright, I need to go back to the village now. Stay safe, youngster.

721990502.text: Are you one of those "advisors" sent by the Lord Commissioner to teach us how to fight our wars? If you are, you can just go look for Lord Masahito.

721990503.text: Saimon Katsumi asked us to come here.

721990504.text: Hmph. You outlanders have no manners. Mr. Saimon is well-respected around here. How could you address him without any honorifics?

721990508.text: ...Alright, I get it. This isn't the time to be arguing about manners.

721990509.text: Since Mr. Saimon trusts you, I should, too.

721990510.text: So, what can I help you with?

721990512.text: Ah, him... he's probably gone off to become a bandit.

721990513.text: Well, for a person of his character, being a bandit is freer than being a soldier.

721990514.text: By the way, don't tell Mr. Saimon this, or he'll get mad.

721990515.text: Jirou actually managed to convinced that scaredy-cat Ishikawa to desert together with him. He made it alright... But Ishikawa ending up eating detention barracks rations for quite a few days!

721990516.text: But even that was because Lord Masahito was kind enough to cover this up and not report it to his accursed old man. If not for that...

721990517.text: *sigh* Let's not even go there... Jirou really got Ishikawa into hot water, I'll tell you what...

721990518.text: If it wasn't for Mr. Saimon, I'd smack him silly the next time we meet!

721990519.text: Well, that's all I know about Jirou. Well, you're going to have to exercise some creativity to make that news a little less unpleasant for Mr. Saimon...

721990520.text: Ah, right. If you'd like to know more, you can go ask Ogura. He's over there by the tower, and was on duty the day it happened. He probably saw more than I did, at any rate.

721990522.text: It was nothing, don't sweat it.

721990523.text: Also, could you not tell Lord Masahito about this?

721990524.text: Jirou was annoying, sure, but this is a matter of life and death. We're not going to go there.

721990602.text: May I ask... what you're doing here in the camp?

721990603.text: If you're not on important business, please leave. This is a key military site. Unrelated persons are not permitted to enter.

721990604.text: I'm here at Saimon Katsumi's behest.

721990605.text: Saimon...? Ah! You mean Saimon Jirou's father!

721990606.text: Sorry for my rudeness, I didn't know that you were here on the old man's request.

721990607.text: I'm not very familiar with Saimon Jirou, but since his family is so worried, I'll do all I can.

721990609.text: That night, I saw him and Ishikawa fleeing northwards. So I followed the usual our private protocol and sounded the alarm after 15 seconds.

721990610.text: Usually, these few seconds would let you find a good spot to hide if you're lucky.

721990611.text: But we never expected that Ishikawa would trip, flip, and fall out of fright... Well, we caught him on the spot.

721990613.text: *sigh* That Ishikawa. I mean, you'd think that he would at least act the part of a samurai scion...

721990614.text: If I don't miss my guess, Saimon Jirou has probably fled to Jinren Island, the northernmost section of Narukami Island.

721990615.text: Bandits who refuse to submit to the Shogunate have gathered there, and have increased in number due to the war.

721990616.text: Now that our attention has been shifted to the Sangonomiya and away from them, they're getting all kinds of uppity ideas.

721990617.text: The latest rumors even say that they've tried to set up their own independent nation, or declare a grand revolt against our great Ogosho... or some crazy nonsense like that.

721990618.text: Well, we weren't very well acquainted, but I do hope that Saimon Jirou hasn't thrown in with those fellows.

721990619.text: Thanks for sharing what you know.

721990620.text: I'm just glad that I could help. I mean, everyone has family they miss.

721990621.text: Ah yes. Could you... refrain from reporting this to Lord Masahito?

721990622.text: The issue with the Lord Commissioner is already giving him enough of a headache. He really doesn't need any more trouble.

721990701.text: You're back. Here, have a few Lavender Melon... save them for the road, if you will.

721990702.text: Ah yes, as for young Jirou... Is there news of him?

721990703.text: (Uh, we should probably avoid telling him what's going on...)

721990706.text: Ah, is that so... If he is well, it is well.

721990710.text: This is good. Ah, my boy truly is a lucky lad. A lucky lad indeed!

721990711.text: Well then! What are you two standing there for? Pack up now, let's go!

721990714.text: Come now! My boy Jirou has experienced so much hardship — I shall go send him some local specialties to pamper him a little!

721990715.text: He must've gone hungry and thirsty many times on the battlefield. Indeed, he must be missing the food back home madly.

721990716.text: And of course, I'll take the opportunity to drop in on Lord Kujou and ask him to "take care" of that useless son of mine, haha!

721990718.text: Y—Yeah... Please calm down, good sir!

721990719.text: Ah, but I am calm. In fact, I am glad! As I shall be, to see my son again...

721990721.text: The battlefield he's on is super dangerous!

721990722.text: Right! That's right! It's super dangerous there. Swords flashing as far as the eye can see, arrows falling like rain, and... and...

721990723.text: Cannonballs as big as Paimon falling down and exploding across the land!

721990401.text: Outlander, what are you doing in the camp? This is a key military location.

721990402.text: ...Well, whatever. It's not as if we haven't seen any outlanders recently or anything.

721990403.text: If you're one of them "advisors" from Narukami Island, look for Lord Masahito directly. He'll welcome you, I'm sure.

721990404.text: Saimon Katsumi asked us to come here.

721990405.text: Sorry, I don't know a Sai— wait, you mean Saimon Katsumi?

721990406.text: Old Man Saimon from Konda Village? That's who you're talking about, right?

721990407.text: Ah, so you're a friend of... I see. My apologies, I was rude. Is the old man still well? I hope he's still spry.

721990408.text: He's very worried about Jirou, his son.

721990410.text: Well, we're quite worried about him too, to be honest...

721990412.text: Mm... Please don't tell the old man... And definitely don't tell Lord Masahito...

721990419.text: Yeah, what's so special about deserting anyway?

721990421.text: *sigh* This war is too much to bear.

721990422.text: We've fought quite a few battles against the rebels recently, and we've lost a lot of comrades. They were all our mutual friends...

721990423.text: Of course, Lord Masahito tried to help us settle our emotions a little, and has assigned us garrison duties as a result.

721990424.text: But the Lord Commissioner has been ordering him to send troops out, which must be frustrating him...

721990425.text: Never mind. Back to Jirou, then... That fellow's always liked those stories about great bandits... "Konda Ikki" or something, that was his favorite.

721990426.text: When you add that up with his being tired of fighting this war... I think it's possible that he might have upped and left to join the nearby bandits...

721990427.text: I'm sorry, but that's all I know. If you want to know, you can go ask Ono. He should know more.

721990428.text: See that guy sitting over there, sighing and hanging his head? That's Ono, you can't miss him.

721990430.text: You're too kind. Say hi to Old Man Saimon for me, would you?

721990801.text: Phew, finally, someone's here to rescue me!

721990802.text: Thank you, thank you so much!

721990803.text: But we can't stay in this place. Let's split up and get out of here!

721990804.text: Ah, right. I know of a safe spot. Let me just mark it out for you over... here.

721990805.text: Just look for me there, got it? Okay. Great. Bye!

721990807.text: Ugh, he's gone off on his own. So rude!

721990810.text: That's true. Let's get out of here first, then!

721990901.text: If you hadn't gotten me out of that cage, those fellows would have turned me into a blood urchin...

721990903.text: Hahaha. Oh right, the two of you are outlanders. You wouldn't know our local parlance.

721990904.text: It's a very scary, ancient method of punishment. A very, very scary one...

721990906.text: Alright, alright, Paimon doesn't wanna hear it! Ugh, why did Paimon even ask!?

721990907.text: #No, wait. Actually, how did you know all this weird stuff, huh, {NICKNAME}?

721990908.text: Hehe. Why don't you try to guess?

721990911.text: #Ah, so {NICKNAME}'s your name. Pleased to meet your acquaintance.

721990913.text: We want to ask you about a couple of things.

721990915.text: So we're looking for a certain Saimon Jirou...

721990917.text: Why'd you want to know where he is?

721990921.text: I... I've heard on the grapevine that the Tenryou Commissioner's sent out lots of ninjas to capture deserters in secret.

721990922.text: Looking at you ask about this and that, I was starting to wonder if the things I heard were true.

721992301.text: I mean, the key's right there! What's stopping you from getting it?

721992302.text: Well, stay in that cage a moment, will you?

721992303.text: Young lad, the world outside your cage has changed greatly since you last saw it...

721992305.text: We must continue to observe you. We must see if you have the qualities necessary to save this world.

721992308.text: Wait, Paimon recognizes you! Lord, this is the very person you saw in your dreams!

721992310.text: Ugh, are you both done yet? Help me get that key already!

721991101.text: My lords! Here, sit, please! Sorry for the trouble...

721991102.text: ...But how goes your search for those stone slates?

721991105.text: Ah, so you must have been successful, then?

721991109.text: This is all of them, right?

721991116.text: What do you mean "one missing"! We worked really hard to find these four!

721991117.text: And now you say that we're missing one—!

721991201.text: How are things going? I can already smell the treasure, haha!

721991204.text: One, two, three, four... Hmm, no, that's not right.

721991207.text: This guy is untrustworthy. He's trying to play us!

721991209.text: D—Don't be so hasty! Let me explain.

721991210.text: I hid one other stone slate beforehand — here, beside a waterfall amidst the cliffs on Ritou's opposing shore. Here, I'll mark it out on your map.

721991211.text: I just need you two to go on one last trip.

721991212.text: Really...? Paimon still thinks this is suspicious.

721991215.text: See, if I didn't have that last slate, I wouldn't be able to get to the treasure either, would I?

721991216.text: Then why didn't you tell us from the start?

721991217.text: Well, I didn't trust you all as much then. But since you've both helped me so much, there's no reason for me to hide anymore.

721991219.text: I'll leave it to you two, then. I'll be resting here. Just look for me again once you've found it.

721991220.text: Hmph. Aren't you a pair of idle hands.

721991221.text: We're doing all the work here... Maybe we should renegotiate our terms!

721991222.text: Wait! We had an agreement on that one! You'll have a majority share!

721991224.text: He's panicked, that's what's for sure.

721991225.text: Well, since you look like you want that treasure so desperately, we'll trust you just this once.

721991226.text: We're definitely gonna renegotiate once we get our hands on that last stone slate.

721991302.text: That's our line. Who are you?

721991303.text: What's that got to do with you?

721991304.text: I will not cut down a nameless person.

721991305.text: Hah! You outlanders have such a rule as well?

721991307.text: There's no need to waste time here, just fight him already!

721991310.text: You've come to save this kid?

721991314.text: We're here to settle a score with him!

721991316.text: I'm here to do just that myself!

721991317.text: In which case, I'm afraid you're going to have to get in line.

721991318.text: Hmm. Would you like to know...

721991321.text: He told me so at least a few times.

721991323.text: He bluffed you into helping him find the stone slate, didn't he? Bet he didn't tell you that the treasure still needs a key to open it, huh?

721991325.text: Hah! You see, the treasury doesn't just have one gate, but three.

721991326.text: Want to open that door? Slates, key, you'll need 'em both.

721991327.text: This fellow is a little snake. Had us all fooled.

721991329.text: How about this? I suggest that you and I settle this whole treasure business between us.

721991330.text: From the looks of you, you aren't with the Shogunate. That suits me just fine. I'd sooner trust an outlander than one of those lackeys.

721991331.text: And if you can prove your ability, I'll let you into my group. It's a good deal for you!

721991333.text: Oh, him? I'll have the dogs tear him to shreds. We'll pack the pieces up and chuck 'em into the sea.

721991335.text: What do you mean by that?

721991336.text: I mean that Toratarou doesn't bite.

721991337.text: And how do you know that?

721991338.text: He's a good dog, he wouldn't bite anyone!

721991339.text: I think you're in need of a few dog bites, alright!

721991340.text: But that's the thing. Toratarou wouldn't bite anyone! He's a real friendly dog!

721991343.text: But, but, but! Just shut up already, or do you need me to smash you, cage and everything!?

721991346.text: You were talking about a key...

721991348.text: That smart aleck thought that he could hide the treasury key and keep all the treasure for himself.

721991349.text: But he was way too hasty for his own good. He's just full of openings!

721991350.text: Now in our line of work, the most important thing is a sense of "fairness."

721991351.text: Things don't end well for those who try to hoard everything for themselves.

721991352.text: It's just the principle of the matter, you know? And when someone doesn't listen to his brothers, then slightly... harder measures are required.

721991353.text: So he fled into the cage, locked himself inside, and threw the key away—

721991355.text: I know, right? He stunned us right into silence too.

721991356.text: And then he gave a cry of shock—

721991357.text: I threw the wrong key... I threw the cage key into the trees opposite us.

721991359.text: Bwahahahahaha! What in the world is that?

721991362.text: So, the person you're trying to save is this hapless, worthless man.

721991363.text: Not much to his character either: he's a deserter, hated by all!

721991364.text: And finally, he even got on the bad side of someone he couldn't afford to offend!

721991365.text: But you on the other hand — you're a smart person. You've got brains, brawn, and you've got your ways.

721991366.text: Between him and I, it should be pretty obvious who you should choose, eh?

subQuests.subQuestName: Find Saimon Jirou on Jinren Island

721991402.text: Noooo! I wanna go home! I don't wanna be a bandit! Or a treasure hunter!

721991404.text: There, there... We're here to rescue. We're gonna take you home.

721991405.text: No! No! I want to live! I still want to see my mother...!

721991410.text: (Just look at him! Paimon doesn't think he's gonna listen to a word you say... We might as well just keep up the act!)

721991411.text: Stop! Stop! Don't come any closer!

721991414.text: You've caused us lots of trouble, and your repeated deceptions are a sin that cannot be atoned for!

721991417.text: You have contributed to the Shogun's righteous cause in aiding in the defeat of these bandits!

721991418.text: By these actions have you thus redeemed yourself, and thus, you shall not be punished. Indeed, we shall bring you home to be reunited with your parents!

721991428.text: Is this... some kind of newfangled interrogation technique?

721991429.text: Pfft! No, it isn't! We're going to bring you home! C'mon, aren't you happy?

721991433.text: Whoa, what are you trying to do, bite someone?

721991434.text: ...So you're saying that not only am I not going to be "dealt with," but that I made a contribution, right?

721991436.text: Hahaha! That's right, that's right! That was my intention all along!

721991437.text: I won't beleaguer you with the details, but I was merely baiting those crooks in when I was captured the previous two times...

721991438.text: I redirected you and intentionally got myself captured, for I had calculated perfectly that you would find me here, just as I fell into the trap!

721991439.text: But little did they know that I had risked myself to serve as the lure while you closed the net! Ah, like the praying mantis hunting the cicada, they did not see th—

721991601.text: What in the world is all this...

721991603.text: We've looked all over the place. Nothing but rotten provisions and old pottery...

721991604.text: Famous swords and armor, precious gems and gold... There's nothing like that here.

721991607.text: Hey! You aren't tricking us again, are you!?

subQuests.subQuestName: Open the "treasury" front door using the key

721991802.text: You little brat! Bet you've been slacking off instead of fighting for Her Excellency like you ought to have, eh? And to top it off, you didn't even have time to write to me!

721991804.text: Working hard at everything but fighting, am I right?

721991808.text: It means you're an old mouth breather...

721991809.text: This kid can always count on your falling for his fibs. But not me — I always see through his little lies.

721991810.text: I'll bet he ran away to have his own little adventures because he thought army life was hard, boring, and dangerous.

721991811.text: ...Just like you when you were young.

721991812.text: Lazy, impatient, and feckless, but fond of a good brag. Ah, you men are all the same...

721991813.text: Hey! Why'd you start trashing me all of a sudden?

721991814.text: Let him speak for himself! What happened?

721991817.text: Hahahahahaha! The what to the what now? What is this nonsense? Hahaha!

721991818.text: I'm ashamed to call you my son!

721991819.text: You should just sod off to be a comedian in the city — and don't come back, you hear?

721991820.text: Hehe, I'm just glad that you didn't lose a limb, Jirou.

721991821.text: Though to be honest, we'd be more relieved if you did...

721991822.text: Whoa. That's a guy's real parents for you, huh...?

721991823.text: Well, again, we're just glad that you came back safe.

721991824.text: After all, you only had to join the army because of that little crime you committed...

721991825.text: Ever since you left, neither we nor the village chief have been able to protect you.

721991826.text: But you've got to learn to look out for yourself, too. How to choose your path wisely, how to assess the risks...

721991827.text: You're a clever kid, but that's not enough when you're away from home. You need to be cautious and...

721991828.text: All right, that's enough nagging, you old fossil. What our boy needs right now is a bath and a good rest.

721991829.text: Um, Paimon heard you mention that he committed a "little crime."

subQuests.subQuestName: Open the stone gate of the "treasury"

721991902.text: How have things gone? Do you have any news?

721991904.text: Ah, to think that I've inconvenienced you so on account of my useless son...

721991905.text: Pick some of the fruits and vegetables around my house before you go. I am old, anyway, and there's no way I could finish them.

721992002.text: You mean our village? Well then, you've certainly asked the right man.

721992003.text: Our village gained its fame from producing dyes, and has been the Shogunate's very own dye production facility for as long as anyone records or remembers.

721992004.text: When business was good in the old days, this place was an ocean of red and purple from here to Byakko Plain.

721992005.text: It's a shame that this is not the case anymore... The young people have gone to the city to seek their fortunes, and with the war going on, we have even more trouble keeping people. We cannot keep them, and we cannot hope for their return.

721992006.text: Even my Jirou has... *sigh* I can only hope that he is doing well.

721992007.text: But if you ask me if I regret sending my boy out to the battlefield...

721992008.text: Haha. We people of Konda Village have never regretted such things.

721992009.text: Our ancestors have never feared any foe, not even during the Archon War those millennia ago.

721992010.text: Half our young men went out to battle alongside the divine kitsune in the war five hundred years ago, and they were all slain, never to return... they were also our ancestors.

721992011.text: Every person here is a descendant of samurai — descendants of the victorious dead and the survivors.

721992012.text: No matter how long the peace or lengthy the prosperity, that memory will never fade.

721992013.text: So... If dying for Her Excellency the Ogosho is to be our fate, we have no reason to refuse.

subQuests.subQuestName: Report back to Saimon Katsumi in Konda Village

721991702.text: You little brat! Bet you've been slacking off instead of fighting for Her Excellency like you ought to have, eh? And to top it off, you didn't even have time to write to me!

721991704.text: Working hard at everything but fighting, am I right?

721991708.text: It means you're an old mouth breather...

721991709.text: This kid can always count on your falling for his fibs. But not me — I always see through his little lies.

721991710.text: I'll bet he ran away to have his own little adventures because he thought army life was hard, boring, and dangerous.

721991711.text: ...Just like you when you were young.

721991712.text: Lazy, impatient, and feckless, but fond of a good brag. Ah, you men are all the same...

721991713.text: Hey! Why'd you start trashing me all of a sudden?

721991714.text: Let him speak for himself! What happened?

721991717.text: Hahahahahaha! The what to the what now? What is this nonsense? Hahaha!

721991718.text: I'm ashamed to call you my son!

721991719.text: Just go and be a comedian in the city — and don't come back, you hear?

721991720.text: Hehe, I'm just glad that you didn't lose a limb, Jirou.

721991721.text: Though to be honest, we'd be more relieved if you did...

721991722.text: Whoa. That's a guy's real parents for you, huh...?

721991723.text: So... are you two really ninjas from the Tenryou Commission?

721991733.text: Hahahaha... All right, give our son a break, you old geezer.

721991734.text: But you've been laughing at me too, mom!

721991735.text: Well, again, we're just glad that you came back safe.

721991736.text: After all, you only had to join the army because of that little crime you committed...

721991737.text: Ever since you left, neither we nor the village chief have been able to protect you.

721991738.text: But you've got to learn to look out for yourself, too. How to choose your path wisely, how to assess the risks...

721991739.text: You're a clever kid, but that's not enough when you're away from home. You need to be cautious and...

721991740.text: All right, that's enough nagging, you old fossil. What our boy needs right now is a bath and a good rest.

721991741.text: Um, Paimon heard you mention that he committed a "little crime."

721990101.text: "It has been over a year since my son, Saimon Jirou, joined the army. He would write letters to us from time to time, and though he has not accomplished much of great note, he would relate everything that happened to him in the army, which comforted this old man's heart greatly."

721990102.text: "The war has continued apace, and my son, who has accomplished little, has stopped sending any letters. This lack of contact has greatly disturbed and wounded this old man's spirit."

721990103.text: "I beseech any who see the notice to help me search for my son. If you know of his whereabouts, whether he ekes out some existence somewhere or has had the fortune of dying for his nation, please let me know, that I may have peace in my heart."

721990104.text: "If you have anything to discuss, I, Saimon Katsumi give you my sincere thanks."

721990301.text: Ho there, youngster! I do not recognize your face. Did you see the notice as well?

721990303.text: Yes, haha. Does it appear like anyone else nearby is young?

721990304.text: Oh dear, where are my manners?

721990306.text: I believe you must have seen that notice earlier. As you may suspect, I am Saimon Katsumi.

721990307.text: (Hey, this has got to be Jirou's "long-winded old man," right?)

721990313.text: Well then, allow me to continue from where we last left off...

721990314.text: It brings me no small amount of shame to ask outsiders to help me find that useless son of mine...

721990315.text: But please, do tell me if you hear of anything regarding him, alright?

721990316.text: No matter if that little brat is alive, or... *sigh*

721990317.text: Please tell me everything you know truthfully.

721991501.text: Phew... I... I'm very sorry, you two.

721991502.text: To tell you the truth, I—I'm still a little frightened by everything that happened...

721991503.text: Oh, forget that for now. We're here for the treasure, y'know? The treasure!

721991504.text: *sigh* Don't... be in such a rush. Just let me take a break, and we'll head off.

721991505.text: Hmph. You can forget about fooling us this time, Jirou!

721991507.text: *sigh* You know what? I'll just give you the key. Just don't lose it now.

721991508.text: And don't worry, it isn't the cage key this time...

721992102.text: Yes? Do you have any news?

721992103.text: Uh, no, not right now! We're still trying to look for him.

721992104.text: Haha, slow down. Don't rush it, youngster.

721992105.text: *sigh* But at the same time, please don't take too long either.

721992201.text: Finally, someone's here... Please, kind souls, get me out of here! I've been stuck here for several days now...

721992202.text: Sure! C'mon, let's bust this thing open in one go!

721992206.text: C—Can you guarantee that this won't hurt me?

721992208.text: Oh come on, we're gonna save you first — everything else can wait!

721992209.text: No! Don't! It's... it's too scary!

721992210.text: And you don't have to be so reckless, I know where the key is!

721992211.text: And you didn't think to tell us that first?

721992213.text: *sigh* If you're here to help, you should listen to what people have to say, at least!

721992214.text: The key's in that tree over there. Just help me get it and open this cage.

721992215.text: See that thing glittering over in that tree? That's where the key is.

721992216.text: I'll thank you all properly once I'm out of here.

721992217.text: Hmm, you threw it pretty far, huh?

721992218.text: How did you end up in here?

721992219.text: It's... a long story, and this isn't the place to chat about that. Get me out of here first and then we'll talk.

721992220.text: Do you know where Saimon Jirou is?

721992221.text: I—I do, yes! I'll tell you once I'm out!

721992402.text: We were just discussing the matter...

721992403.text: Do you outlanders need to hold a meeting just to get a single key?

721992404.text: Ah, but what if you are some sort of great bandit?

721992405.text: Perhaps it would be safer if you remained inside that cage.

721992406.text: That's true... What if he starts growing super huge all of a sudden once we let him out, and he tears us to pieces and eats us, all snicker-snack-like?

721992407.text: Hey! That's not what a bandit does!

721992411.text: Oh no! A werewolf! So scary...

721992412.text: Are you two playing me for a fool here?

721992501.text: The key is in that tree, so stop playing around already!

721992502.text: Come on, haven't you heard of "mental strength"?

721992503.text: I just know that it has nothing to do with this cage.

721992504.text: And that's where you'd be wrong!

721992505.text: First, you need to create an imaginary space.

721992506.text: Then focus your attention on the cage around you, and imagine it disappearing... and disappearing...

721992513.text: Talking to you is bad for my mental health.

721992514.text: So, starting from now, I'm just not going to speak to either of you.

721992515.text: Aw, come on, don't be like that!

721992601.text: Oh, you're back? Don't worry about the stone slates. Once you've found them, just give them all to me at once.

721992702.text: Ah, yes, about that... I do have something I'd like you to help me with.

721992703.text: The camp also keeps a little dog. Hehe, we got on pretty well — you could even call us cellmates in a way...

721992704.text: Could you... help me rescue that little fellow?

721992705.text: I remember that the key should be on Red Nose Tsutomu.

721992706.text: He's always drunk out of his gourd... There's no missing him.

721992801.text: So, do you know a Saimon Katsumi...

721992805.text: I didn't enjoy being in the army. And you've seen how the old man gets when he talks about war...

721992806.text: But you know what? He's lived in peace all this time himself, and he never dared to join the army either... So he just pushed those unfulfilled expectations onto me.

721992807.text: As for me... I was okay with it at first, too. The Tenryou Commission treated us well, and I was making good money!

721992808.text: But then, the real war started up...

721992809.text: Well, the battlefield follows its own logic, of course. But the gain was never worth what we lost.

721992810.text: I couldn't get with that kind of thinking, so I left.

721992812.text: By which he means that he deserted.

721992814.text: Come on, "deserting" is such a bad word. I prefer something like...

721992820.text: Right, I remember now. This is what we call "transferring investments!"

721992822.text: He means going off to become a bandit.

721992824.text: How did you know that I—

721992828.text: Alright, alright. Let's not talk about this stuff... We'll have all the time in the world to talk nonsense once the stone slates have all been found.

721992902.text: Well, you continue then. If you'd like to rest for a while over here, that's fine too.

721993002.text: How is it? How goes your search.

721993005.text: Y—Yes, I'm sorry! I spoke out of turn, out of turn!

721993006.text: Please, my lords, rest your weary feet here, and continue on your way once you are rested as you please...

721993102.text: So you've been quite idle here, huh?

721993103.text: Haha, there's no need to put it like that.

721993104.text: Sit as you please and have something to eat. This tent of mine isn't too bad, I hope!

721993105.text: Ah, yes. How goes the search for the stone slates?

721993108.text: So quickly? Ah, I should have expected no less from travelers from abroad who move as they please through Inazuma!

721993109.text: No need to rush. At this rate, the day I get rich is not far off, I'd wager!

721993111.text: Aye, what say we all get rich together, eh?

721993301.text: I'm Saimon Jirou! I'm Saimon Jirou, alright?

721993302.text: The treasure's all yours! I won't take a single Mora!

721993303.text: (Let's not get him too much more worked up than this. He's such a wretched guy...)

721993401.text: If you hadn't gotten me out of that cage, those fellows would have turned me into a blood urchin...

721993403.text: Hahaha. Oh right, the two of you are outlanders. You wouldn't know our local parlance.

721993404.text: It's a very scary, ancient method of punishment. A very, very scary one...

721993406.text: Alright, alright, Paimon doesn't wanna hear it! Ugh, why did Paimon even ask!?

721993407.text: #No, wait. Actually, how did you know all this weird stuff, huh, {NICKNAME}?

721993408.text: Hehe. Why don't you try to guess?

721993411.text: #So you're called {NICKNAME}. My name is Saimon Jirou. Pleased to meet you.

721993413.text: Hmm. That's right, we still don't know how you ended up in that cage.

721993414.text: Well, this is a bit embarrassing... But I was just trying to get some peace of mind from my naggy old father...

721993415.text: Never thought I'd wander right into a nest of bandits and get myself kidnapped!

721993416.text: If not for you, I'd be in mortal danger for sure!

721993417.text: Ah, yes, I forget. I should probably give you some reward for this deed. My apologies.

721993421.text: I'm sorry, but I can't give it to you right now.

721993422.text: Come on, then why did you leave us hanging like that?

721993423.text: Whoa, no need to rush. Just slow down a bit and let me talk.

721993424.text: Well, I—I'm a professional treasure hunter.

721993425.text: Professional treasure hunter? Never heard of that...

721993426.text: Uh, I mean, I'm someone who looks for treasure for a living.

721993428.text: After some lengthy investigation, I've discovered the location of some treasure nearby.

721993429.text: It's just that the treasury gate requires four stone slates to open.

721993431.text: So you want us to run your errands for you?

721993432.text: C'mon, don't be so hard up! If you bring the stone slates to me, and let me open the treasury door for you, I won't take a single Mora. The treasure will all be yours.

721993434.text: I mean, you did save my life! What's some treasure compared to that?

721993435.text: I can't be sure if we can trust you...

721993436.text: Hehe, ah, see I knew you'd be too kind to take it all.

721993437.text: How about this, then? We'll split it thirty-seventy. Seventy for me, twenty for you, and we'll give that last ten to the Ogosho in taxes. How about that?

721993438.text: Hey! Why do we have to split the loot with the Shogun?

721993440.text: It's a huge treasury, you know? Even twenty percent is a sizable amount!

721993441.text: And it's better than getting nothing, am I right?

721993442.text: Didn't you say that you weren't going to take a single Mora?

721993443.text: Hehe, that was a limited-time offer — you snooze, you lose!

721993445.text: We'll settle this score once we find that treasure, mark Paimon's words!

721993501.text: Please go, you two. Time waits for no one!
